w:r.w:t: UI Presentation Only — No Backend Changes

DO NOT TOUCH: database, schema, tables, API contracts, validation engines, scoring engines, services, business logic, events, backend calculations, blueprint bridge, signal calculations, condition engine.
DO NOT CHANGE: any endpoint URL, any request payload shape, any response shape. The data layer is frozen.
ONLY CHANGE: the React component file(s) that render validation results. CSS/Tailwind classes, JSX structure, copy text, interaction handlers, expandable states. Nothing else.

Read the existing validation results page completely. Map every variable name that holds validation data. Use those exact same variables in the new render. Do not rename, restructure, or re-fetch anything.

Every piece of data the validation engine calculated must be translated into plain human language before it reaches the screen. The user should never see a score formula, a technical term, or an internal label.
A plain sentence: 'Good idea. A few changes could make this stronger.'
A confidence ring with label: 'How strong this looks today'
'Here is what we found about your idea.'
'Who else is already doing something similar?'
Remove entirely — never show these to users
Not shown on this page — only on blueprint picker
Every technical term must be replaced. Apply this table across every label, heading, tooltip, and description on the page.
Who else is already doing this
Things that could slow you down
Reality check / How strong this looks
A different direction may work better
The type of economy you are in
How much work this will take
How long trust takes to build here

Build these sections in this exact order. Each section is a self-contained React component or block within the validation results page. All data comes from the existing validation object already in scope.
Top card — the headline verdict in human language + confidence ring.
Show what was entered. Let user confirm or redirect the meaning.
Demand, crowdedness, growth — all plain language.
Demand signal translated to simple High/Medium/Low.
Things that could slow you down
Final decision cards. Not recommended path — user chooses.
A full-width card at the top of the page. White background. Green left border (4px).
Large headline sentence derived from the verdict value. Font size: 28px. Bold. Dark gray.
"Good idea. People want this. Keep going."
"Good idea. A few changes could make this stronger."
"This can work — but your current direction makes it harder."
"This needs some changes before it's ready to build."
Below the headline: one sentence of context. Example: 'Based on your goal, your situation, and current market signals.'
Below that: expandable section — 'Why does it say this? ▼'
When expanded, show plain language explanation using these data points:
validation.reality_score → never shown as a number — shown as context only
Example expanded text: 'You are based in the United States. You selected high commitment. You are building a SaaS business. These factors increased how strong this looks.'

Confidence ring — SVG donut. Value = Math.round(validation.reality_score * 10). Label above ring: 'How strong this looks today'. Small text below ring: 'Based on your goal, situation, and market signals'.
Ring colour: 0-39 = red, 40-59 = orange, 60-74 = yellow, 75-89 = green, 90-100 = dark green.
NEVER show: Proceed / Adjust / Pivot / Blocked as labels. NEVER show the raw score number on its own. NEVER use the word 'validation'.
'Let us make sure we understood you correctly.'
Your goal
Your reason
Show 3 cards with slightly different framings of what the goal could mean. Derived from validation.purpose_decomposition. Each card has a radio-style selector.
If purpose_decomposition is null or empty, show 3 generic framings of the goal text.
Below the 3 cards: 'Does one of these feel more accurate? Selecting one will not change your results — it helps us explain things better.'
Selecting a card: saves selection to local state only. Does not trigger any API call. Does NOT rerun validation.

'Who else is already doing something similar?'
Sub: 'Knowing who is already winning helps you find where to stand out.'
Data source: validation.competitor_analysis — take first 3 items.
If competitor_analysis has fewer than 3 items, show available ones. Never show empty cards.
First letter of competitor.name in a colored circle. No images — use initial only.
competitor.strategicGapForUser — 1 sentence. If empty show: 'Gap analysis not available for this competitor.'
Plain language tip derived from competitor.archetypeContext
X button top right — closes modal
NEVER use the words: competitive intelligence, competition pressure, market position, competitive landscape.
Section 4 — What the Market Looks Like
Sub: 'Understanding the space you are entering.'
Yes, growing (7+) / Slowly (4-7) / Not right now (<4)
Each tile is tappable. Opens an inline expansion below the tile:

Demand expanded: 'People in [location] are already paying for similar solutions. This means there is real appetite for what you want to build.' OR 'Interest exists, but getting people to pay requires extra work in this area.'

Crowdedness expanded: 'A few strong players are already established. This is not a reason to stop — but it means you need a clear reason to stand out.' OR 'The space is open. Fewer competitors means more room to grow.'

Growth expanded: 'This type of business is growing right now. Good timing.' OR 'This space has slowed down recently. Starting earlier would have been better, but there is still opportunity for the right angle.'
'What if I was in a different country?' → opens Section 8 (Try different versions) pre-scrolled to country field.
'What if I targeted a different audience?' → opens Section 8 pre-scrolled to audience field.
'What if I changed my price?' → opens modal with pricing angle suggestions from validation.economy_briefing.
Section 5 — Do People Actually Want This
Sub: 'The most important question. Demand tells you if there is a real problem to solve.'
3 options: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW. Show whichever applies (derived from market_score).
HIGH (score 7+): large green text. 'People in your area are already buying similar solutions.'
MEDIUM (score 4-7): large orange text. 'Some interest exists, but converting that interest to paying customers takes more work.'
LOW (score < 4): large red text. 'Low signals of people paying for this in your area right now.'
Below the indicator — two expandable cards:
Card 1: 'What makes demand higher here?' — bullet list from validation.market_analysis.demandFactors or from industry_intelligence data.
Card 2: 'What could lower demand?' — bullet list from risk factors relevant to demand.
Section 6 — Things That Could Slow You Down
Sub: 'These are not reasons to stop. They are things to plan for.'
Source: validation.industry_cons array. Show up to 5 items.
Each card: warning icon (orange), plain language title, 1 sentence description.
Plain language mapping for common risk types:
Too many people already doing this
This takes longer than most people expect
You may need more money than you think
Your audience is not clearly defined yet
People are not desperate to solve this yet
Building trust takes time in this area
There are rules to follow in this space
Each card is tappable. Opens inline expansion:
Why: plain explanation of the risk in 2-3 sentences.
How to reduce it: 1-3 actionable plain language suggestions.
'Apply this suggestion' button: adds a note to local state that user acknowledged this risk. Does NOT call any API. Shows a green checkmark on the card.
Section 7 — If This Was Your Money
'If this was your money, would you back it?'
Sub: 'Think of yourself as your own investor. These are the questions a smart backer would ask.'
HIGH/INTENSE → 'Yes, based on your commitment.' MEDIUM → 'Likely, with discipline.' LOW → 'This may be challenging at your current pace.'
Yes (7+) / With the right model (4-7) / Hard at this stage (< 4)
Could this grow beyond your area?
